To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NDF is sufficient to cause terminal end bud persistence and mammary adenocarcioma formation, and that it may do so through activation of the erbB3 pathway.

NDF induces persistence of TEB structures in the mammary epithelium of transgenic mice, that NDF induces mammary adenocarconomas in a small percentage of transgenic mice and that NDF induces benign Harderian gland tumors in transgenic mice.

(1) overexpression of Ndf in the mouse mammary gland leads to the formation of terminal end bud structures, which are normally lost by 8 weeks of age in the mouse mamary gland, and (2) overexpression of the NDF ligand in the mouse mammy gland leads to the development of mammary tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of NDF in normal development of the mammary gland and in mammary tumorigenesis, and the signal transduction mechanisms involved.
the role of the neuregilin/erbB family of growth factors in mammary development and tumorigenesis.
the role of NDF and the erbB receptor family in the mammary epithelium and the Harderian gland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NDF is sufficient to induce TEB persistence and adenocarcincomas and necessary to induce Harderian gland hyperplasia in the mammary epithelium of transgenic mice.

overexpression of an NDF-like protein in the mammary epithelium of transgenic mice results in a phenotype that is characterized by a persistent TEB structure, the appearance of mammary adenocarciomas, and Harderian gland hyperplasia.

the MMTV-Ndf gene is not a sufficient oncogene, but is sufficient to induce terminal end bud persistence in the mammary epithelial cell and is necessary to induce adenocarcinoma formation in this organ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NDF, when targeted to the mammary glands, can induce both benign and malignant tumors in this organ.
NDF is a potent mitogen in the mammary epithelium, but that the signal transduction pathway it activates is not sufficient to cause a fully malignant phenotype.
NDF is a mitogenic factor for mammary epithelial cell in vivo and can induce both benign and malignant tumors in the mammary tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NDF is a potent mitogenic and differentiative factor for the mammary epithelium.
NDF, a member of a family of growth factors, can act as a potent oncogene when expressed in vivo.
overexpression of the ligand NDF, a member of the epidergmal growth factor (EGF) family, is sufficient to cause mammary gland hyperplasia and carcinomas in transgenic mice.
